blocks.md: Welcome to **Conclusion** (Vol III). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

An autonomous agent combines several systems disciplines (foundation models, memory hierarchies, isolated execution sandboxes, transactional event logs, and independent verifiers) in one closed-loop control architecture. Each component can pass its own tests, yet the system can still fail if the contracts between components are missing or unclear. The core challenge of agentic systems engineering is designing the deterministic harness that bounds and verifies a stochastic proposer, a problem that larger models and more elaborate prompts do not remove.
